knowledge.statement: MemoryStorage::get_entries and get_suffix subtract self.trimmed_idx from the caller-supplied index without any guard, and trim subtracts it in the same way when computing how much to drain: a request for a prefix below the trimmed index therefore aborts the caller on the subtraction in an overflow-checked build, and when overflow checks are disabled the subtraction wraps, the wrapped index lands past the end of the log and the read reports an empty result - the silently empty suffix rather than an error. Observed for the suffix and the range read in receipt 9daa1fc530244c7ea0863a1d73d90960.
knowledge.conditions: Any call into the shipped in-memory storage with an index below the index it has already trimmed to, whatever the caller: the library's own log-sync path is closed to that case inside a cluster (the trim bound is the minimum recorded accepted index and the snapshot path takes its own branch), so the remaining callers are direct users of the Storage trait or storage implementations' own code. Observed in receipt 9daa1fc530244c7ea0863a1d73d90960, which appended four entries, trimmed two (log length 4 then 2, events 0 and 1) and then read below the trimmed index: get_suffix(1) and get_entries(0, 1) both aborted (suffix_below_panicked and entries_below_panicked true at event 1, with the process naming memory_storage.rs:103 and memory_storage.rs:93), while get_suffix(2) at the trimmed index returned ok with two entries. The profile matters: the panics rest on overflow checks being enabled, which the recorded build has, and other implementations of the trait may differ in either direction.

interpretations.rationale: Witnessed and bounded, with the second producer recorded and with both halves of the suffix route now covered - one by execution inside the cluster and one by execution at the storage. The trim witness stands: with recorded accepted indexes drifted to 10, 9 and 7 over six indices of content and every node's decided report at 9, trim(None) returned no error and compacted index 7, past the leader's own content, after which its reads of indices 5 and 6 reported Trimmed (ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a events 9-15). The discriminator this question carried asked whether a producer other than trim can raise a compacted index past a replica's content, and the snapshot receipt answers that it can: with the same drifted state, snapshot(Some(8), false) returned Ok, advanced the leader's compacted index to 8 and produced a snapshot holding none of the five decided entries (e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5). That second producer needs no recorded accepted index at all - its bound is the leader's decided index - so a drift confined to the decided index would be enough for it, while trim additionally needs the drifted value to be the configuration's minimum recorded accepted index; both are bounded by values the leader derives for itself. Correction review: the drift knowledge this account cites was narrowed to revision 2, which keeps the half this account needs - the reported accepted index drifts one further index per re-synchronization round, inflating exactly the recorded accepted indexes the trim bound is derived from - and bounds the decided index to the rounds in which a write quorum of drifted reports covers it; this account reads its decided values from its own receipt's samples, so the narrowing leaves its conclusion unchanged, and the use is re-read at revision 2 below. The suffix route, now in three parts. Executed in-cluster: in the snapshot-capable sibling case the lagging replica re-synchronized below the leader's compacted index (the leader had compacted to 8 with a snapshot holding zero ids) was not refused and did not panic - it received that complete snapshot and no suffix, reported accepted 10 / decided 10 and read two decided entries where the configuration decided six (0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 152-162). Closed by source: a request below a trim-produced compacted index cannot arise inside the cluster, because the trim bound is the minimum over the leader's accepted_indexes vector and that vector carries an entry for every configuration member from the start (get_min_all_accepted_idx, util.rs 186-191, whose expect message reads Should be all initialised to 0, and set_promise rewrites the sender's entry on every promise), so only a replica's own inflation moves the bound. Executed at the storage: a caller that does ask the shipped in-memory storage for a prefix below its trimmed index is aborted rather than answered - with four entries appended and two trimmed (log length 4 then 2, receipt 9daa1fc530244c7ea0863a1d73d90960 events 0 and 1) both get_suffix(1) and get_entries(0, 1) panicked, the process naming memory_storage.rs:103 and memory_storage.rs:93, the two unguarded self.trimmed_idx subtractions, while get_suffix(2) at the trimmed index returned ok with two entries; when overflow checks are disabled the same subtraction would wrap past the end of the log and the read would report an empty result instead, so the outcome is a property of this implementation and build profile rather than a library guarantee. The abort this lineage did observe through the protocol belongs to a different entry point, the public snapshot call on a NoSnapshot instance (40ab66a5c5c847619ae2ff68b85641e7-question-1).

b26c13954e184cd2b9fdfda975aff136-gap-4.explanation: Resolved for every route the gap names. In-cluster (executed): a replica re-synchronizing below a compacted index is not refused and does not panic - it is handed a complete snapshot built from the empty part of the log and a shortened decided log (receipt 0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 152-162, guarded result event 162 with panicked false). A peer compacted while its recorded values were still truthful (closed by source): impossible, because the trim bound is the minimum of the leader's recorded accepted indexes over a per-node vector that is initialised for every member, so a truthful replica keeps the bound at or below its own accepted index. A store-level trim or a direct range read below a compacted index (executed): the shipped in-memory storage aborts the caller instead of returning an empty suffix - with four entries appended and two trimmed (log length 4 then 2, receipt 9daa1fc530244c7ea0863a1d73d90960 events 0 and 1) both get_suffix(1) and get_entries(0, 1) panicked, the process naming memory_storage.rs:103 and memory_storage.rs:93, the unguarded subtractions of the trimmed index, while the read at the trimmed index itself returned ok with two entries. The one caveat left in the answer is the profile, not the route: with overflow checks disabled the same subtraction would wrap past the end of the log and the read would report an empty result, so a release-style build of this implementation answers the gap's alternative rather than the panic, and a different storage implementation is free to do either.

knowledge.assertion: trim accepted a drifted bound and compacted past the content the leader held
the snapshot path accepted a drifted bound and produced a snapshot holding none of the entries
trim's bound is the minimum over a per-node recorded accepted vector, so a truthful replica keeps it at or below its own accepted index
the reported accepted index drifts one index per re-synchronization round while the decided index follows only while a write quorum covers it
a replica re-synchronized below the compacted index receives a complete snapshot built from the empty range
a read below the trimmed index aborts in the shipped in-memory storage under overflow checks, and would wrap to an empty result without them

counterevidence: Every node's decided report had also drifted to 9, so the documented all-decided precondition was satisfied only in the drifted bookkeeping; the obligation I rely on is that the compacted index must not exceed the entries the leader holds, which it did (7 for trim, 8 for the snapshot).
The trim call returned Ok, so nothing in its own result signals the over-compaction; the witness is the compacted index together with the content sampled before and after.

The in-cluster route below a compacted index is executed rather than argued, and it does not abort: the lagging replica was re-synchronized with a complete but empty snapshot and a shortened decided log (0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 161, 162), so the over-compaction of this account leads to a silent loss on a lagging replica; the abort seen in the same lineage belongs to the public snapshot call on a NoSnapshot instance and is recorded under its own question.

The peer-side sub-route is closed by source rather than merely untested: a truthful replica's recorded accepted index stays in the minimum the trim bound is taken from, so the bound cannot pass such a replica and no request below the compacted index follows from it.

The storage-level abort is a property of the shipped implementation and the build profile, not of the library: the trait leaves out-of-range reads to the implementer, the probe's panics rest on overflow checks being enabled, and the same call in a build without them would return an empty result instead.
limitations: The trim over-compaction is bounded to replicas whose recorded accepted index has drifted; a truthful replica would have kept the bound lower, and the per-node initialisation of the recorded vector is the reason.

The storage-level answer is executed for one profile and one implementation: the probe ran in the overflow-checked build this run has used throughout, where both reads below the trimmed index abort, while the wrapping alternative is reasoned from the same unguarded subtraction and was not built or run; other implementations of the trait may differ in either direction.

Comparison 1 of the probe receipt came out unknown because its declaration named at_state while the emitted field is suffix_at_state, so the at-the-trimmed-index observation is asserted from the sampled event rather than from a comparison outcome; the declaration slip does not affect the panic flags, which are carried by the same event.

The baseline comparisons of the trim and snapshot receipts are unknown because they were admitted through event names shared across cases in one execution; those states are asserted from the sampled operands.

One three-node configuration, three reconnection rounds, one leader change for trim and one snapshot-capable entry type were exercised; the peers that receive a forwarded compaction were not sampled beyond their accepted and decided indexes, and the lagging-replica outcome was observed with the leader's log empty above its compacted index.

For the trim path the observed over-compaction is the minimum of the drifted recorded values, so the number of indices it passes beyond the leader's content depends on how many rounds each replica drifted; only one such combination was sampled.

The initialisation claim for the recorded accepted vector is read from the source's own expect message and from set_promise rewriting the sender's entry; no execution sampled the vector directly or ran a trim while one member had never promised.
